title: The Problem of Ignoring the Ignorability Assumption in Advertising Measurement: A Matrix Completion Solution
package_mismatch_note: The archive stored under this suffix belongs to a different Marketing Science paper: README header 'Visual Plant Imagery and Property Valuation: A Descriptive Analysis' by Yuqian Chang, Nathan Fong, Ning Ye, Maureen Morrin (Marketing Science, 2026). It contains a realtor survey (SPSS) and house-sale listing data (data_raw(n=40294).csv) with Stata code (code_main.do) regressing log sale price on counts of plant images with zipcode FE. Nothing relates to advertising auctions or matrix completion.
eligible_reason: Not eligible. (i) The paper (OpenAlex abstract) frames overlap violations in algorithmic ad allocation as a missing-data problem and proposes a matrix completion estimator for ad effects in observational auction data; this is a methods paper on ad-impression-level causal estimation, not a staggered-adoption DiD (and matrix completion is not an admitted modern DiD estimator under 5b). (ii) The package under this suffix belongs to a different paper (cross-sectional hedonic regressions of house prices on plant-image counts with zipcode FE, also not a DiD).
design_notes: Intended paper: no package available here. Shipped (mismatched) package: Stata reg/xtreg fe i(zipcode) of ln_price on plant_sum_gpt and listing controls; cross-section of 31,031 sold properties.
data_files_note: No data for the intended paper. The mismatched package ships house-listing data with masked IDs and prices shifted by a random constant plus Gaussian noise (README masking table).
data_provenance_note: Intended paper's data not shipped; the mismatched package's data are disguised (perturbed prices, recoded IDs).
screener_notes: Screened from package and OpenAlex abstract (no article text). Lead may want to add this suffix to data/package_mismatches.txt; the plant-imagery paper is itself cross-sectional and would not qualify.
